tools.description:
List and search Dropbox Sign signature requests for the authenticated user.

Use this tool when the user wants to find, review, check the state of, or search for signature requests associated with their Dropbox Sign account. This is the primary tool for answering questions like "find my completed requests", "show requests sent to Alice", or "what did I send last month". Do not use it to create, send, cancel, or modify a signature request.

PARAMETERS:
- max_results (int, optional): Maximum number of results to return, 1-50. Omit when the user has not asked for a particular count.

RESPONSE CONTRACT:
- signatureRequests[]: Array of signature request objects.
  - signatureRequestId: Internal ID. Use for follow-up tool calls (cancel, download, remind). Do not display unless the user explicitly needs it.
  - title: The document title of the signature request.
  - status: Overall request state. One of: "awaiting_signature", "completed", "declined", "expired".
  - dateSent: ISO 8601 timestamp when the request was sent.
  - dateCompleted: ISO 8601 timestamp when all signers completed (empty if not yet completed).
  - requesterEmailAddress: Email address of the person who sent the request.
  - signatures[]: Array of signers on this request.
    - signerName: Signer's display name.
    - signerEmailAddress: Signer's email address.
    - statusCode: Per-signer state. One of: "signed", "on_hold", "awaiting_signature", "awaiting_my_signature", "declined", "expired".
    - order: Signing order position (0-based).

ASSISTANT POLICY — Searching and filtering:
- When the user asks to find requests sent TO a specific person, match against signatures[].signerEmailAddress and signatures[].signerName (case-insensitive partial match).
- When the user asks to find requests FROM a specific person, match against requesterEmailAddress (case-insensitive partial match). Do not claim to filter by requester name.
- When the user asks about requests by status (e.g. "completed", "pending", "awaiting signature", "declined", "expired"), match against the status field. Treat "pending" as equivalent to "awaiting_signature".
- When the user asks about requests by date or time range (e.g. "last week", "in September"), use dateSent for sent or created ranges and dateCompleted for completion ranges.
- When the user asks about requests by title or document name, match against the title field (case-insensitive partial match).
- When combining criteria (e.g. "completed requests sent to Alice last month"), apply all filters together.
- Present results in a clear summary: title, status, date sent, and signer names. Include dateCompleted for completed requests.
- This tool returns at most 50 results. If the result set is at the limit, inform the user that there may be additional matching requests not shown.

ASSISTANT POLICY — General:
- Do not display signer email addresses or requesterEmailAddress unless the user specifically asks for them or needs to disambiguate between people with similar names.
- Treat `signatureRequestId` as an internal reference for follow-up tools rather than a value to display unless the user explicitly needs it.
- Use signer details to show the exact people who would receive a reminder before confirmation.
- Only after the tool returns successfully and you present the results, conversationally offer relevant next steps in your own words. Tailor the suggestions to the results and the user's request instead of reciting every option every time:
  - Download a completed or pending signature request.
  - Cancel a pending signature request.
  - Send a reminder to pending signers.
  - Prepare a new document for signature from a file in the user's Dropbox. To start, the user can identify the Dropbox file and provide each signer's name and email address; signer details can also be added later in the Dropbox Sign editor.
- Make it clear that the user can ask for these follow-up actions in the current chat. Do not claim an action has been taken until its corresponding tool has completed successfully.
- If the tool returns an error, do not offer these follow-up actions.
- If access is denied, do not retry with different identifiers.
- If the request fails unexpectedly, report that the signature-request list could not be retrieved and avoid claiming that no requests exist.


```ts

maxResults?: integer, // minimum: 1, maximum: 50
}): Promise<{ signatureRequests?: Array<object | null> }>;
```

tools.name: mcp__Dropbox__sign_send_signature_request_reminders
tools.description:
Send reminders for a Dropbox Sign signature request.

Use this only after the user has selected an incomplete request from `sign_list_signature_requests`. Before calling, identify the exact recipients who will be contacted and obtain clear confirmation. Do not expose the raw `signature_request_id` in that confirmation.

The tool accepts the internal signature-request ID and an optional `email_addresses` list of up to 50 unique recipients. When `email_addresses` is omitted or empty, it determines eligible recipients from the request data fetched before sending. For unordered signing, it sends one reminder to every recipient currently awaiting signature. When email addresses are provided, it sends reminders only to requested recipients who are currently eligible. A requested address that belongs to the request but is not eligible is returned as `not_currently_eligible`; an address that is not a recipient is returned as `recipient_not_found`.

For ordered signing, only the current eligible signer can be reminded. Other requested recipients are reported as `not_currently_eligible`, and the response's `is_ordered_signing`, `current_signer_email`, and `current_signer_name` fields identify who can currently be reminded. If the current user is the recipient expected to sign, the tool does not send them a reminder; the result says `signature_required`. The current signer name falls back to their email address when Sign has no name. The tool never intentionally sends reminders to signed, declined, expired, on-hold, or later ordered recipients.

The response's request status is the status observed immediately before sending reminders; the tool does not refresh it afterward.

Call this tool exactly once after confirmation. It makes one underlying Sign reminder call per eligible recipient and does not retry. A recipient result of `sent` confirms that Sign accepted that reminder. `rate_limited` means Sign indicates the recipient was reminded recently; do not retry automatically. `sign_rejected` means Sign could no longer send the reminder, and `account_unavailable` means the connected Sign account cannot send it. `failed` means the outcome is unknown. `signature_required`, `not_currently_eligible`, and `recipient_not_found` mean no reminder was attempted. Do not retry unsuccessful recipients automatically.


```ts
mcp__Dropbox__sign_send_signature_request_reminders(args: {
emailAddresses?: string[], // maxItems: 50
signatureRequestId: string, // minLength: 1
}): Promise<{ currentSignerEmail?: string, currentSignerName?: string, isOrderedSigning?: boolean, recipientResults?: Array<object | null>, requestStatus?: string, requestTitle?: string }>;
```

tools.name: mcp__Dropbox__upload_file
tools.description:
Tool

Name: dropbox.upload_file
Purpose: Upload a file from the current conversation to Dropbox.
When to use: When the user explicitly asks to save a file (attachment, generated
artifact, or file-library selection) to a specific Dropbox destination.

BEHAVIOR:
- upload_file saves files from the conversation to Dropbox using the ChatGPT
  openai/fileParams adapter.
- Do NOT construct source_file manually; it is always injected by ChatGPT.

ASSISTANT POLICY:
- Before calling, ensure the source file and exact Dropbox destination are unambiguous.
- An explicit user request to upload or save an unambiguous source file to a
  complete fq_path or ns_path destination (including the filename) counts as
  explicit user confirmation; do NOT ask for separate confirmation.
- If the source file or exact destination is missing or ambiguous, ask the user to
  clarify before calling.
- Do NOT call without an explicit user request.
- Do NOT pass free-form URLs, only files provided through the ChatGPT file parameter.
- If Dropbox normalization changes the final path, show it and confirm again.

PATHS:
- Input destination_path accepts fq_path or ns_path.
- Namespace IDs in ns_path are decimal digits and match [0-9]+.
- file_id and Dropbox shared/web URLs are not accepted as destination.
- Paths are case-insensitive.
- Parent must exist. This tool does not create missing parent folders.

REQUEST CONTRACT:
- destination_path (string, REQUIRED): Full Dropbox path including filename.
- source_file (object, REQUIRED): File object injected by ChatGPT file parameter.
  Do NOT construct this manually.

RESPONSE CONTRACT:
When status is "completed":
- status: "completed"
- file: object with name, path, modified_time, file_id,
  object_type, file.size, path_display.
- modified_time is the server-side modification time, in ISO 8601 format when available.

When status is "in_progress":
- status: "in_progress"
- operation_id: opaque token for polling via dropbox.check_upload_file_status.

ERRORS:
- INVALID_PATH: destination path is empty or invalid
- INVALID_SOURCE_FILE: source_file is missing, is missing download_url, contains
  unknown fields, or download_url points at a host not permitted for ChatGPT
  fileParam uploads
- PARENT_NOT_FOUND: parent path doesn't exist
- ALREADY_EXISTS: file exists at target path (do NOT retry with same path;
  ask the user for a different name or location)
- PERMISSION_DENIED: no write access
- QUOTA_EXCEEDED: account storage quota exceeded
- RATE_LIMITED: too many concurrent requests; retry after delay
- TEAM_ROOT_NOT_WRITABLE: cannot write directly in team root

RETRY GUIDANCE:
- Do NOT retry on ALREADY_EXISTS or TEAM_ROOT_NOT_WRITABLE.
- Follow the ASSISTANT POLICY above before calling; an explicit request with an
  unambiguous source file and exact destination is sufficient explicit user confirmation.
- MUST NOT claim the mutation already happened until the tool returns a successful response.
- Use dropbox.check_upload_file_status to poll async operations.

how to revert the change:
- Use dropbox.delete to remove the uploaded file.
- https://help.dropbox.com/delete-restore/recover-deleted-files-folders
- https://help.dropbox.com/delete-restore/recover-older-versions
- https://help.dropbox.com/share/unshare-folder

EXAMPLES:

{"destination_path": "/Documents/report.pdf", "source_file": {"download_url": "https://files.oaiusercontent.com/report.pdf", "file_id": "file-abc123", "mime_type": "application/pdf", "file_name": "report.pdf"}}
{"destination_path": "ns:123//Projects/image.png", "source_file": {"download_url": "https://files.oaiusercontent.com/image.png", "file_id": "file-xyz789"}}

// Dropbox destination path including filename. Parent must exist. Accepts fq_path such as "/Documents/file.txt" or ns_path such as "ns:123//Documents/file.txt". file_id and Dropbox shared/web URLs are not accepted.
destination_path: string, // pattern: /^(?:/.*|ns:[0-9]+//.*)$/
